+1  # Currencies
+2
+3  An invoice is written in one currency, and every amount on it is in that
+4  currency. Amounts are kept as whole numbers of the currency's minor unit: cents
+5  for euros, pence for pounds, and yen themselves for yen, which have none.
+6
+7  ## Which currency an invoice is in
+8
+9  1. The currency the request names, if it names one.
+10 2. Otherwise the customer's preferred currency, if they have one.
+11 3. Otherwise `DEFAULT_CURRENCY`, which is EUR unless it is set.
+12
+13 An invoice whose lines are in another currency than its own is refused.
+14
+15 ## Supported currencies
+16
+17 | Code | Name | Minor units | Shown as |
+18 |---|---|---|---|
+19 | EUR | Euro | 2 | €1,234.56 |
+20 | GBP | Pound sterling | 2 | £1,234.56 |
+21 | USD | US dollar | 2 | $1,234.56 |
+22 | JPY | Japanese yen | 0 | ¥1,234 |
+23 | CHF | Swiss franc | 2 | CHF 1,234.55 |
+24 | SEK | Swedish krona | 2 | kr 1,234.56 |
+25 | KWD | Kuwaiti dinar | 3 | KD 1,234.567 |
+26
+27 ## Tax

+5  export const CURRENCIES = {

+7  	GBP: { minorUnits: 2, symbol: '£', name: 'Pound sterling' },
+8  	USD: { minorUnits: 2, symbol: '$', name: 'US dollar' },
+9  	JPY: { minorUnits: 0, symbol: '¥', name: 'Japanese yen' },
+10 	CHF: { minorUnits: 2, symbol: 'CHF ', name: 'Swiss franc' },
+11 	SEK: { minorUnits: 2, symbol: 'kr ', name: 'Swedish krona' },
+12 	KWD: { minorUnits: 3, symbol: 'KD ', name: 'Kuwaiti dinar' }
+13 } as const;
+14
+15 export type CurrencyCode = keyof typeof CURRENCIES;
+16
+17 export function isCurrencyCode(text: string): text is CurrencyCode {
+18 	return Object.hasOwn(CURRENCIES, text);
+19 }
+20
+21 /** A currency code as a person or a client wrote it: " eur" is EUR. */
+22 export function parseCurrency(text: string): CurrencyCode {
+23 	const code = text.trim().toUpperCase();
+24 	if (!isCurrencyCode(code)) {
+25 		throw new RangeError(
+26 			`Unknown currency "${text}". Use one of ${Object.keys(CURRENCIES).join(', ')}.`
+27 		);
+28 	}
+29 	return code;
+30 }
+31
+32 export function minorUnits(code: CurrencyCode): number {
+33 	return CURRENCIES[code].minorUnits;
+34 }
+35
+36 export function symbol(code: CurrencyCode): string {
+37 	return CURRENCIES[code].symbol;
+38 }
+39
+40 /**
+41  * Rounds an exact amount of minor units, such as a tax, the way the currency
+42  * requires: half away from zero, except Swiss francs, which are rounded to the

+45 export function roundForTax(exact: number, code: CurrencyCode): number {

sections.title: Money carries its currency
sections.summary:
New `src/currency.ts` lists the seven supported currencies (minor units, symbol, name) with `parseCurrency`, `minorUnits`, `symbol` and `roundForTax`. `src/money.ts` replaces the branded `Cents` number with a `Money` object `{ minor, currency }`; `add` throws `CurrencyMismatch` across currencies, `sum` now needs the currency so an empty sum has one, and `inMajorUnits` is added for display.

Look at:
- `roundForTax` (src/currency.ts +45..+48): the CHF branch uses plain `Math.round`, which rounds halves towards +∞, so negative CHF amounts don't round half away from zero like the other currencies do.
- `multiply`/`percentOf` (src/money.ts +43..+49) still use `Math.round` too, so negative halves round differently from tax.

sections.title: Tax is rounded the way its currency requires
sections.summary: `taxFor` (src/tax.ts +8..+11) works out the exact tax in minor units and rounds it with `roundForTax`, so CHF tax goes to the nearest five rappen. It no longer goes through `percentOf`. The tests add a CHF case.

sections.title: Invoices have one currency, and show it
sections.summary:
`Invoice` gets a `currency` field (src/invoice.ts +17..+18). Totals are summed in that currency, and `validate` refuses any line priced in another currency (+50..+52). `src/format.ts` moves to `src/format/amount.ts`, and `formatAmount` now prints the currency symbol and the right number of decimals (none for JPY, three for KWD). The PDF prints an "Amounts in …" line (src/pdf/render.ts +16).

The PDF snapshot was re-recorded: every amount gets a € prefix, and there is a new JPY snapshot. Note that `src/format/amount.ts` still holds `formatDate`/`formatQuantity`, so the name `amount` is a little narrow.

sections.title: Storing the currency: migration and stores
sections.summary:
Migration 004 adds `invoices.currency` (backfilled to EUR, then the default is dropped), renames `invoice_lines.unit_price_cents` to `unit_price_minor`, and adds a nullable `customers.preferred_currency`. `InvoiceStore` reads and writes the currency and builds line prices in it. `CustomerStore.preferredCurrency` is new.

- The column rename breaks any instance still running the old code while the deploy is under way.
- `preferred_currency` is `CHAR(3)` with no check, and `preferredCurrency` (src/store/customers.ts +24..+30) passes it on as a `CurrencyCode` without validating it.

sections.title: API: choosing the currency, and GET /currencies
sections.summary:
`POST /invoices` picks the currency in this order: the one in the request (parsed in any case, 422 if unknown), then the customer's preferred one, then `config.defaultCurrency` (src/server/routes.ts +30..+38). Responses gain `currency` and `gross_minor`. The new `currencyRoutes` serves `GET /currencies`. `unit_price_cents` is renamed to `unit_price_minor` in the request, which **breaks existing clients**, though the spec only bumps to 1.5.0.

finalState.overview:
Ledger moves from euro-only to **multi-currency invoices**, and from console output to **structured JSON logging**.

1. **Money carries its currency.** `Cents` becomes `Money { minor, currency }`, backed by a new table of seven currencies in `src/currency.ts`. Combining two currencies throws an error.
2. **Tax rounding** goes per currency: half away from zero, and CHF to the nearest five rappen.
3. **Invoices** get one currency. Lines priced in another currency are refused, and amounts are formatted with their symbol and the right number of decimals (format.ts moves to format/amount.ts). The PDF names the currency.
4. **Storage:** migration 004 adds the invoice currency (existing invoices become EUR), renames `unit_price_cents` to `unit_price_minor` and adds the customer's preferred currency.
5. **API:** the currency comes from the request, then the customer's preference, then `DEFAULT_CURRENCY`. There is a new `GET /currencies`. The request field rename breaks existing clients.
6. **Logging:** `createLogger` with levels and per-request fields, set by `LOG_LEVEL`. `src/log.ts` and `src/config.ts` now import each other.
7. Docs, then housekeeping: vitest bump, release script, logo, smoke test.

Things to look at first: the config/log import cycle, the hand-edited-looking `src/generated/api-types.ts`, the breaking `unit_price_minor` rename, and the package.json version still being 1.4.0.

sections.title: Money carries its currency
sections.summary:
New `src/currency.ts` lists the seven supported currencies (minor units, symbol, name) with `parseCurrency`, `minorUnits`, `symbol` and `roundForTax`. `src/money.ts` replaces the branded `Cents` number with a `Money` object `{ minor, currency }`; `add` throws `CurrencyMismatch` across currencies, `sum` now needs the currency so an empty sum has one, and `inMajorUnits` is added for display.

Look at:
- `roundForTax` (src/currency.ts +45..+48): the CHF branch uses plain `Math.round`, which rounds halves towards +∞, so negative CHF amounts don't round half away from zero like the other currencies do.
- `multiply`/`percentOf` (src/money.ts +43..+49) still use `Math.round` too, so negative halves round differently from tax.

sections.title: Tax is rounded the way its currency requires
sections.summary: `taxFor` (src/tax.ts +8..+11) works out the exact tax in minor units and rounds it with `roundForTax`, so CHF tax goes to the nearest five rappen. It no longer goes through `percentOf`. The tests add a CHF case.

sections.title: Invoices have one currency, and show it
sections.summary:
`Invoice` gets a `currency` field (src/invoice.ts +17..+18). Totals are summed in that currency, and `validate` refuses any line priced in another currency (+50..+52). `src/format.ts` moves to `src/format/amount.ts`, and `formatAmount` now prints the currency symbol and the right number of decimals (none for JPY, three for KWD). The PDF prints an "Amounts in …" line (src/pdf/render.ts +16).

The PDF snapshot was re-recorded: every amount gets a € prefix, and there is a new JPY snapshot. Note that `src/format/amount.ts` still holds `formatDate`/`formatQuantity`, so the name `amount` is a little narrow.

sections.title: Storing the currency: migration and stores
sections.summary:
Migration 004 adds `invoices.currency` (backfilled to EUR, then the default is dropped), renames `invoice_lines.unit_price_cents` to `unit_price_minor`, and adds a nullable `customers.preferred_currency`. `InvoiceStore` reads and writes the currency and builds line prices in it. `CustomerStore.preferredCurrency` is new.

Look at:
- The column rename breaks any instance still running the old code while the deploy is under way.
- `preferred_currency` is `CHAR(3)` with no check, and `preferredCurrency` (src/store/customers.ts +24..+30) passes it on as a `CurrencyCode` without validating it.

sections.title: API: choosing the currency, and GET /currencies
sections.summary:
`POST /invoices` picks the currency in this order: the one in the request (parsed in any case, 422 if unknown), then the customer's preferred one, then `config.defaultCurrency` (src/server/routes.ts +30..+38). Responses gain `currency` and `gross_minor`. The new `currencyRoutes` serves `GET /currencies`. `unit_price_cents` is renamed to `unit_price_minor` in the request, which **breaks existing clients**, though the spec only bumps to 1.5.0.

Look at:
- `src/generated/api-types.ts` is marked generated, but `api/openapi.yaml` defines none of the response schemas it now has (`currency`/`gross_minor` on InvoiceResponse, `preferred_currency`, `CurrencyResponse`, `CurrencyListResponse`). So it looks hand-edited, which is why I moved it into this section. It also types `currency` as a required key that can be `undefined` rather than as optional.
- A failed `preferredCurrency` lookup (a DB error) lands in the same catch, so it comes back as a 422 (+36..+38).
- `fakeCustomers` in `src/test-helpers.ts` supports the new tests.

sections.title: Structured JSON logging, with a configurable level
sections.summary:
`src/log.ts` swaps the `log`/`warn` console helpers for `createLogger`: JSON lines on stderr, levels, and `with` for per-request fields. All of `src/config.ts` is here, including `DEFAULT_CURRENCY`, which the API section uses. The call sites move to the new API: app, routes, the invoice store and `totals` in src/invoice.ts (cross-referenced).

Look at:
- **Circular import:** `src/log.ts` imports `config` and builds `log` at module load (+1, +59), while `src/config.ts` imports `isLevel` from `log.ts` and calls it at module load (+2, +19..+23). In ESM, whichever loads first will probably hit a TDZ error: either `config` is not initialised yet or `ORDER` is not. Worth running the app to check.
- 'invoice not found' in the store went from warn to info (src/store/invoices.ts +32).
- The refused-invoice warning now logs only how many problems there were, not what they were (src/server/routes.ts +53).

sections.title: Docs: currencies and logs
